Professional Summary

I am an M.S. candidate in Aquaculture and Aquatic Sciences at Kentucky State University. My thesis tests how salt type and salinity affect growth and gene expression in olive flounder raised in recirculating systems. Before KSU, I studied alternative protein and lipid sources in fish feeds at Sylhet Agricultural University in Bangladesh.

About

I am a Graduate Research Assistant at Kentucky State University, advised by Dr. Andrew J. Ray, on a USDA Evans-Allen project that develops practical methods for more productive and sustainable marine aquaculture. My thesis trial runs olive flounder (Paralichthys olivaceus) across salt types and salinities in 16 recirculating tanks, with sampling every two weeks. I measure growth and survival, run gill and liver histology, and analyze gene expression by qPCR.

Alongside the flounder work, I raise Pacific white shrimp at high density in a 20 m³ intensive saltwater raceway, monitor water quality across our systems, and grow microalgae, Ulva and Salicornia on aquaculture sludge to measure nitrogen and phosphorus recovery.

My interest in feeds started in Bangladesh. For my first M.S., I formulated diets with fermented mustard oil cake and fermented soybean meal for climbing perch and presented the results at Aquaculture America 2025 in New Orleans. I also tested black soldier fly larvae oil for butter catfish. I am now looking for PhD and research positions where fish physiology, nutrition and production systems meet.

Publications

Peer-reviewed work and conference talks

MDPIAnimals2026 · 16(2)
Featured publication

Evaluation of Different Terrestrial Oils as an Alternative to Dietary Fish Oil on Feed Physical Properties, Growth, Feed Utilization, and Fatty Acid Profile of Gangetic Catfish (Mystus cavasius)

A 70-day feeding trial comparing fish oil with soybean, black soldier fly larvae, palm and mixed oils. The mixed-oil diet gave the best growth, and feed efficiency did not differ among diets.

doi.org/10.3390/ani16020330
